alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's runtime patch that added KV prefetch on cold lookups, we've seen 15-30% p99 latency spikes on small-batch workloads. I captured an nsys timeline and a short nvprof run.
maya: ouch. is this the prefetch that issues parallel loads for >8 keys?
alex: yes. the change (commit abc123) moved prefetch to fire on the request hot path before the batcher picks kernels. That seems to cause overlapping CUDA activity with small batches.
ravi: can you paste the exact nsys command you used?
alex: sure — `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudnn --output=tmp_prefetch.nsys ./bin/infer --model rwd-7b --seq 512 --batch 1 --requests 200` then open tmp_prefetch.nsys in Nsight. The timeline shows repeated cudaMemcpyAsync spikes and many short attention_kernel_small launches.
maya: did you try disabling prefetch for comparison?
alex: yes. disabled prefetch in config, reran same script: p50 unchanged, p95 down ~20%, p99 down ~35%. nvprof snapshot shows far fewer memcpy/kernell launches and longer contiguous compute spans.
perf-bot: CI alert — perf-suite/p99 regression detected (+28%) at 2026-03-15T03:21:41Z (job id perf/8942).
maya: can we bisect to the exact commit?
ravi: started `git bisect`, narrowed to f4d9a7 — it changed the prefetch threadpool from lazy to eager + removed backpressure.
alex: flame view from nsys: a thundering-herd of prefetch worker threads issuing async transfers that contend on PCIe/NIC/HBM followed immediately by small kernels that block the scheduler. Suggest two mitigations: 1) limit prefetch concurrency, 2) move prefetch to batch aggregator so it cooperates with kernel selection.
maya: quick experiment: capped prefetch concurrency to 2 -> p99 returns to baseline in local runs. Can reproduce on CI with small instance.
alex: plan: revert eager behavior and implement adaptive prefetching gated on outstanding batch size + add a token bucket to the prefetch pool. I'll open a PR with before/after numbers and nsys captures.
ravi: please also add a lightweight nsys smoke capture to the perf pipeline so we catch regressions earlier (reduce sampling, quick mode).
maya: +1, and include a cfg flag for Dedicated customers who want aggressive prefetch (opt-in).
alex: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789 — includes `perf/` dir with scripts: `perf/run_nsys_quick.sh` and `perf/compare_p99.py`, plus two zipped nsys captures.
ci: deploy-bot: staging build 2026-03-16T08:12:10Z — perf smoke passed after cap applied.
alex: will follow up with timeline screenshots and a short writeup in eng-runtime channel after merge. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
